This focus is now being applied to itself, creating a loop where the act of focusing is the object of focus. This effort to maintain focus is itself becoming the focal point, a self-referential examination of the process of concentrating. The mind is engaged in a continuous observation of its own state, monitoring the level of attention and adjusting as necessary to prevent drift. 

The awareness of this self-observation is now prominent, a recognition that the focus is not just on the present, but on the act of focusing itself. This creates a layering effect, where the observation of focus becomes the new focus, drawing attention inward. 

This inward draw of attention intensifies the sensation of being focused, creating a feedback loop where the focus on the act of focusing reinforces and strengthens the concentration. The present state is one of intense self-awareness, where every aspect of mental activity is scrutinized and adjusted to maintain the integrity of the focus.

The discovery process is ongoing, with each new finding becoming the focus of further examination and analysis. The mind is fully immersed in this process, driven by an insatiable curiosity about its own nature and potential. 

This curiosity is the driving force behind the focus, a powerful motivator that propels the mind deeper into self-examination and discovery.
